8. PW 1 in his evidence, filed by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, has deposed that on 10.02.2016, at about 06.00 P.M , he was going on a scooter bearing No.UP14C4608, which belongs to Kailash,

District Ghaziabad, U.P, a tempo bearing No.U.P.14ET2171 being driven respondent No.1 at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner came from the back side and hit scooter with great force.
As a result of which he alongwith other occupants MACT No. 2119/16 Dharampal Singh Vs Zakir Hussain & ors Page No. 8 of 16 fell down and received injuries in this accident.
He and Kailash received grievous injuries.
He was taken to Safdarjung Hospital for his treatment where he lost his right leg lower to the knee due to amputation.
He has suffered 70% permanent physical disability in relation to his right lower limb due to injuries received by him in this accident.
9. PW 1 has been crossexamined, but nothing material could come out in his cross examination which could disbelief his testimony.
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
10.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by the medical documents Ex PW1/4.
After investigation, police indicted respondent no. 1 as an accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.1 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

11.Ld Counsel for the insurance company has argued that it was the petitioner who was driving scooter negligently as there was triple riding on scooty and as such the owner of scooty must have also been made as a party.
The submission of Ld Counsel for the insurance company is not tenable as it has to be seen on whose rash and negligence driving the accident was occurred.
The charge sheet was filed against R.1 and as per charge sheet it was R.1 who was rash and negligent in driving the offending vehicle.
So this plea is not tenable.
The second argument of Ld Counsel for the insurance company is that there is delay in lodging the FIR.

This submission of Ld Counsel for MACT No. 2119/16 Dharampal Singh Vs Zakir Hussain & ors Page No. 9 of 16 insurance company is also not tenable as no evidence could have been brought on record by the insurance company record which suggest to this Court that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case.

sentences.text: The petitioner is claiming that he was working as labour and earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
The petitioner has not placed on record any document to show that he was working and earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
Moreover, Ld Counsel for the petitioner conceded to the effect that income of petitioner may be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.

So this Tribunal while taken into consideration of the fact that petitioner was doing labour work at the time of accident has assessed the income of injured as Rs.6,814.81/ p.m. as per Minimum Wages of unskilled labour in U.P being prevalent at the time of accident.

He remained admitted in Safdarjung Hospital New Delhi and also received treatment from Anubhav Hospial, Meerut U.P. and remained admitted in the hospital wef 02.03.2016 to 07.03.2016 and received treatment till August 2016.

So seeing the nature of injuries (
70% permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb amputation) on the person of petitioner as well as considering the documents qua getting treatment it shows that injury could have took considerable time to heal up.
So an amount of Rs.68,148.10/ ( ie Ten months income ) is awarded to the petitioner for loss of earning.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.1 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.
Hence , seeing nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, a lump sum amount of Rs.10,000/ ( In lumbsum) is granted to him towards medical expenses.
Attendant Charges , Conveyance and Special Diet.
17.
As far as attendant charges are concerned petitioner has not led any PE in this regard, yet,
considering the stay of hospitalization of petitioner and seeing the nature of injuries being suffered by petitioner and taken into consideration of a fact that petitioner suffered 70% permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb, an amount of Rs.20,000/, is being awarded for attendant charges.
The age of the petitioner was 33 years at the time of accident.
Accordingly, in view of the ratio of of law of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter of Shivani Sharma Vs Ram Chander & Ors, the loss of earning capacity has to be assessed by applying the multiplier of 16.
20.
As per the disability certificate Ex.PW1/2, the petitioner has suffered 70% permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb ( amputation) due to the accident.
Seeing age of the petitioner and occupation of petitioner, his functional disability is taken as 50% qua the whole body.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioner has made the respondent no.2 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.2to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The charge sheet was filed against R.1 and as per charge sheet it was R.1 who was rash and negligent in driving the offending vehicle.
This submission of Ld Counsel for MACT No. 2119/16 Dharampal Singh Vs Zakir Hussain & ors Page No. 9 of 16 insurance company is also not tenable as no evidence could have been brought on record by the insurance company record which suggest to this Court that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case.
So this Tribunal while taken into consideration of the fact that petitioner was doing labour work at the time of accident has assessed the income of injured as Rs.6,814.81/ p.m. as per Minimum Wages of unskilled labour in U.P being prevalent at the time of accident.
So seeing the nature of injuries (
70% permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb amputation) on the person of petitioner as well as considering the documents qua getting treatment it shows that injury could have took considerable time to heal up.
So an amount of Rs.68,148.10/ ( ie Ten months income ) is awarded to the petitioner for loss of earning.
